Ground

What you are looking at

A live state from the rules engine, not a mock-up: the field above was generated from a seed, the units were deployed by the composition rules, and every number in the command bar is the engine's own breakdown. Click any unit to inspect it. Hover ground for its rules. Switch fields at the top to see three generated battlefields, none of them a rectangle.

Painted direction for the ground

Two concept paintings for how finished battlefields should read at the war-table zoom: mountain passes, drowned marsh, trenches, fords, ruins. The in-game hexes above use the same palette so the switch from painting to play stays quiet.

Ground rules

Costs are movement points to enter. Defence and ranged bonuses apply to the unit standing on the hex. Climbing one elevation tier adds one point for ground units.

Three decisions before this scales

Map look

Painted hex fills with a faint scratched grid, as above, or a fully painted ground plate with the grid shown only on hover. The engine is indifferent; the art budget is not.

Command bar

Hammered iron with leather straps, portrait in scorched wood, slate ability tiles, parchment tooltips. Confirm or redirect the material language before it is applied to menus and army builder.

Field size

These fields are about 300 hexes with two platoons a side plus specialists. Larger companies need 450 to 600 hexes and a zoomed camera; say which scale the vertical slice should target.
